diffuseAlbedo.source: Palette.json: accent.pavonazzetto realMaterial (violet-veined white marble, Afyon-Iscehisar)
diffuseAlbedo.note: The white ground a little dimmed and cooled by its violet veins, averaged over a face: a first value read from trade photographs until a specimen is measured.

refractiveIndex.source: Substances/cream-marble.json: optics.specularF0 (0.0533, calcite grains in random orientations)
refractiveIndex.derivation: n = (1 + sqrt(F0)) / (1 - sqrt(F0)), the index whose normal-incidence reflectance is the record's F0

porosity.source: Arel Stone (Turkey), 'Afyon Violet Marble' product technical data: porosity 0.2 %, water absorption 0.1 %, density 2.73 g/cm3, http://www.arelstone.com/en/DetayAfyonMenekse.aspx
porosity.note: Verified on the page, which names no test standard. The identity of Afyon Violet with pavonazzetto rests on the project's own Palette.json (accent.pavonazzetto realMaterial: 'traded today as Afyon violet', Afyon-Iscehisar, the site of the ancient Docimium quarries). The proposal also cited an IUGS Heritage Stone designation and literature saying the breccia is more porous. I did not open or verify either, so both are dropped. A specimen test to TS EN 1936 on the violet breccia would settle the value.

wettingDepth.source: Palette.json: accent.pavonazzetto realMaterial (violet-veined white marble, Afyon-Iscehisar)
wettingDepth.note: As the Crema Marfil: a dense stone wets only its outer millimetre.

grain.source: Palette.json: accent.pavonazzetto realMaterial (violet-veined white marble, Afyon-Iscehisar)
grain.note: Crystalline calcite a few tenths of a millimetre across, as a white marble.

bed.source: Palette.json: accent.pavonazzetto realMaterial (violet-veined white marble, Afyon-Iscehisar)
bed.note: The breccia's clasts and the violet veins between them, a first spacing read from trade photographs.

bedAspect.source: Palette.json: accent.pavonazzetto realMaterial (violet-veined white marble, Afyon-Iscehisar)
bedAspect.note: The veins run drawn out, as a column shaft is cut along them.

hurst.source: Candela et al. 2012, Journal of Geophysical Research 117, B08409 (fault surfaces, 0.6 to 0.8; cited in Stone.ush)
hurst.note: The middle of the range measured on rock surfaces, as the travertine's.

toneSpread.source: Palette.json: accent.pavonazzetto realMaterial (violet-veined white marble, Afyon-Iscehisar)
toneSpread.note: Deep violet veins across a white ground: a wide tonal spread.

roughnessSpread.source: Workings/honed.json: unverified surface.microRoughness (no filtered roughness read)
roughnessSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(roughness) across a worked face, as the travertine's.

absorption.source: Substances/cream-marble.json: optics.subsurfaceReference.absorption (Jensen, Marschner, Levoy & Hanrahan 2001, a white marble, measured)
absorption.note: Its white ground is crystalline calcite: the measured white marble stands in until a Pavonazzetto is measured.

scattering.source: Substances/cream-marble.json: optics.subsurfaceReference.reducedScattering (Jensen, Marschner, Levoy & Hanrahan 2001, a white marble, measured)
